The owned spec tests/sprint-05-orient-search/not-found-search-recovery.spec.ts carries the locked token on 5 tests x chromium-desktop/mobile/nojs (15 cases) covering run-specific unknown /docs/ URLs, served-vs-emitted manuscript equality, the 300ms island-clock open independent of index readiness, keyboard navigation to /components/message at HTTP 200, Escape focus restoration, shared production Pagefind resources and Message destination between ordinary and recovery pages, manuscript-query exclusion of every recovery URL, theme retention through the real ThemeToggle, and the no-JS readable plain-link journey. RED was captured via run_flow.py --expect red (15/15 genuine failures, no infra failures) at tests/sprint-05-orient-search/evidence/FLOW-SHELL-16-not-found-search-recovery/proof.red and run.red; GREEN finished 15/15 with run_flow.py --expect green verdict 1/1 PASS (exit=0, artifact_fresh=true, surface_ok=true, coldboot_ok=true, red_proof_ok=true) and the run.json artifact written by the playback itself.
deviations: The JS-only 'Search the site' control ships hidden and is revealed by the page script only when the rnr-search-dialog element is defined (404.astro script block) — the task composed the action but did not specify its no-JS presentation, and hiding it is what keeps AC-1's must_not_observe 'disconnected search trigger' true on the no-JS project.

Added a scoped .not-found :global([hidden]) { display: none } rule in 404.astro because Button's own scoped display:inline-flex beats the UA [hidden] rule and components/ is write-prohibited, so the fix had to live in the consuming page.

Timing independence is proven by the island's own activation clock (__rnrSearchLastOpenMs <= 300ms); a readyAtOpen=false sub-assertion was removed because loadPagefind() starts synchronously right after showModal and can legitimately settle before the observation round trip lands.

Content oracles use specific regions (.page-header__description, .callout__title, main section[data-section="usage"], .family-grid via allInnerTexts with a >=5-families count) instead of generic body/main roots — the surface lint's GENERIC_ROOT_ORACLE findings forced this and the assertions got stronger as a result.

run.json is written by the spec's test.afterAll during every playback (search-contract.spec.ts precedent) because run_flow's artifact_fresh means the declared artifact must be created/changed by the run itself; the separate manifest.json is the agent-authored summary.

The manuscript's bullet links (Introduction, Browse components) are realized as the recovery action set (Search the site, Components, Registry) per the task's R5 region table and AC-4 destinations rather than rendering the raw markdown list; title, explanation and hint are consumed verbatim and asserted byte-equal.
waitForURL patterns and pathname assertions are trailing-slash-agnostic because astro preview serves /components and /components/ both at 200 with no redirect, so anchor hrefs land without a slash.
concerns: Inherited run-order hazard: any astro build wipes dist/pagefind; the task-owned indexer (pnpm exec tsx scripts/docs-data/search-index.ts) must run after the last build before any preview-backed lane — CI owns this ordering, and local reruns must preserve it.

The spec pins current page shapes by design: .family-grid and the >=5 families count on /components, section[data-section="usage"] on item pages, [data-docs-nav] on /docs/introduction, and .page-header__description/.callout__title on the recovery page — a region rename in those surfaces is a deliberate spec-breaking change, not drift to absorb silently.

The HTTP 404 status assertion on unknown paths is local astro-preview behavior, labeled as such in the spec and manifest; deployed Cloudflare not_found_handling and status-code proof remain with the cloudflare specialist and are not claimed here.

The locked 8-step sequence now needs the search dialog dismissed (Escape) before the theme step because a still-open modal dialog blocks clicks on header controls; future edits that reorder steps should preserve that ordering.
findings: Playwright page.evaluate callbacks cannot reference module-scope constants — serialization drops closures and the selector becomes a runtime ReferenceError; inline selector literals in the callback or pass them as evaluate arguments (fixed in inputIsFocused and recoveryTriggerIsFocused).

A Button whose scoped class sets display:inline-flex overrides the UA [hidden] rule, so a hidden attribute alone does not hide it; Astro also scopes descendant selectors, so the fix must be .not-found :global([hidden]) rather than a plain scoped [hidden].

astro preview serves both /components and /components/ at 200 with no redirect, so real anchor clicks land on the exact href spelling — waitForURL regexes and pathname expectations must be slash-agnostic.
A still-open native modal <dialog> blocks clicks on anything outside it (top layer) — Playwright waits on actionability for the full test timeout; dismiss the dialog before touching header controls.

run_flow.py's artifact_fresh means the declared flow artifact must be created or changed by the gate playback itself; the spec writes it in afterAll (hashes via createHash over the real sources, with an 'absent' fallback that the reviewer should treat as a red flag).

This session's display channel garbled identifier words in shown file content and even in typed probe strings; the working discipline was deriving probe strings from real sources with python, trusting tsc/playwright/biome exit codes over displayed text, and byte-anchored replaces verified by grep line numbers (recorded in project memory).
feedback: The run.json-in-afterAll pattern from search-contract.spec.ts is what makes run_flow's artifact_fresh satisfiable at all; worth stating explicitly in TASK-TEMPLATE's evidence section so future implementers do not rediscover it through a failed gate (cost me one extra full gate cycle).

The GENERIC_ROOT_ORACLE surface lint rejects bare body/main innerText oracles; documenting the accepted specific-oracle patterns (named region classes, section[data-section], allInnerTexts aggregates) in the e2e policy README would save implementers a lint-fail cycle.
